title: Retrying fetch client in Node.js
idea: In a Node.js service the API client wraps `fetch` with a per-attempt timeout and jittered retries, and sends an Idempotency-Key so a retried POST never charges twice.
points: `AbortSignal.timeout` cancels an attempt that takes too long.
Retry 502, 503, 504 and timeouts, and only for safe requests.
The server stores each Idempotency-Key's result and replays it on a repeat.
Interview follow-up: retries at every layer multiply; retry at one layer only.

hero.title: A retried charge with a key

messages.label: charge order A
messages.note: The caller passes a key built from the order, so every retry carries the same one.

messages.label: POST /charges, key pay-A
messages.note: Attempt 1. The server creates the charge and stores it under the key.

messages.label: reply lost (demo sends 503)
messages.note: The charge is stored, but the reply never arrives as a success. The demo fakes this with a 503; on a real network it is usually a timeout.

messages.label: wait with jitter
messages.note: The request has a key, so it is safe to repeat. The client backs off first.

messages.label: POST /charges, key pay-A
messages.note: Attempt 2 sends the same key and the same body.

messages.label: 200 stored charge (replay)
messages.note: The server finds the key and replays the stored charge with 200. Nothing new is created.

messages.label: charge CH-1
messages.note: The caller sees one success, and the customer is charged once.

code.title: fetch client, Express server
code.caption: A local Express service fails on purpose. The client recovers a GET, gives up on a slow one, and retries only the keyed POST.

walk.text: /flaky fails twice then works; /slow answers after 500 ms, too late for the client.
Each order's first reply is lost after the charge is made. A known key replays the stored charge.
A seeded generator makes the jitter identical on every run.
Safe means an idempotent method, or a request that carries a key.
Each attempt gets its own 100 ms timeout; a timeout becomes a result, not a crash.
Stop on success, unsafe requests or the last attempt; otherwise back off with jitter.
Four calls, then count how many charges the server really made.

pitfalls: Never retry a POST without a key; order B's charge exists, but the caller saw 503.
Interview follow-up: share breaker state per instance or in a store, and say which.
Interview follow-up: cap retries with a budget, such as a share of total traffic.

quiz.q: What does the last line of retry-client.mjs print?
quiz.why: Order A is created once; its retry replays the stored charge by key. Order B is created once and never retried.

takeaway: Time out every attempt, retry with jitter, and key every retried write.
